answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy is mostly an economics problem. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a comet the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single crystal of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a nadir of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Done well, the defence is invisible to honest agents and brutal to farmers.
